newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Faulding aims for second half boost.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Faulding aims for second half boost.

text.p: F.H. Faulding and Co Ltd said on Monday it was aiming for a first half profit for the year to June 30, 1996/97 similar to last year, but with a significant improvement in the second half.
"We would be aiming for a first half profit similar to last year," chief executive Ed Tweddell told reporters after the annual meeting in Adelaide.
"We do know that the profit expectation for the second half is significantly over the first half because of this anticipation of new products, particularly in the U.S.," Tweddell said.
Tweddell said the announcement earlier on Monday of U.S. Federal Drug Administration approval of the anticonvolsant drug Clonazepam gave Faulding access to a US$260 million market.
The product was in production and should be on the U.S. market by the start of 1997 although the company was disappointed that another generic product had been launched a month ago.
Tweddell said he could not put a number to the earnings prospect of the drug, but said it was a very good market sector in which to be.

"It is a good sized product. It is almost in the blockbuster sales (range) so therefore there are real opportunities for us to establish some good sales and profits of our own in this market," Tweddell said.
He said Faulding's expectations were very strong for profit recovery in its U.S. business, Faulding Inc.
"I think we have started to see that," he said.
"We see the U.S. business after its difficult few years ... as really turning around and becoming a very significant profit contributor to the whole Faulding group."
Tweddell said Faulding was not anticipating any major further acquisitions in its consumer health products business but was always interested in product opportunities.
